chunks: Al-Tawhid: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ya'qub al-Sarraj who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): One of our companions claims that Allah has a form like that of a human, and another says that He is in the form of a beardless youth with very curly hair! Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) fell down in prostration, then he raised his head and said: Glory be to Allah whom there is nothing like Him. Vision cannot reach Him. Knowledge cannot encompass Him. He does not give birth, for an offspring resembles his parent. He was not born so that He could resemble one who came before Him. He will never have among His creatures any rival. Elevated is He from the description of the one who equates Him - a great elevation.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological response to divine corporeality (tajsim) based on Imam al-Sadiq's narration?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kulayni's al-Tawhid records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responding to the Mu'tazili-influenced debate on divine corporeality (tajsim) by prostrating in gratitude for Allah's transcendence. He recites key Quranic verses to refute physical attributes, emphasizing that Allah is unlike creation, beyond visual perception, and free from lineage or generation. This narration is central to Shia theology in affirming Allah's absolute unity and incorporeality.

en.ammaar-muslim: 8. [8/336] al-Tawhid: Ibn al-Mutawakkil from al-Himyari from Ibn Isa from Ibn Mahbub from Ya’qub al-Sarraj who said:

I said to Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: One of our companions claims that Allah has a form like that of a human and another says that He is in the form of a beardless youth with very curly hair! Abu Abdillah عليه السلام fell down in prostration then he raised his head and said: Glory be to Allah whom there is nothing like Him. Vision cannot reach Him. Knowledge cannot encompass Him. He does not give birth for an off-spring resembles his parent. He was not born so that He could resemble one who came before Him. He will never have among His creatures any rival. Elevated is He from the description of the one who equates Him - a great elevation.
